subject: Business Models
title: Platform Switching Moments
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Platform Switching Moments.

hook.text: People rarely switch platforms voluntarily. It takes a crisis to break the loyalty loop.

buildup.text: Major platform switches happen during technology shifts: mobile killed desktop platforms, cloud killed on-premise.

discovery.text: iPhone's launch was a switching moment. Nokia and BlackBerry had loyal users—until a better paradigm arrived.

twist.text: AI may be the next switching moment. ChatGPT reached 100 million users in 2 months—faster than any platform.

climax.text: Switching moments are rare but decisive. Incumbents fall and new giants rise in technology transitions.

punchline.text: Loyalty is strong until a paradigm shifts. Then everything changes.

quiz.question: What typically triggers a major platform switch?

details.summary: Switching moments are events or conditions that create windows for users to move between competing platforms. Technology transitions, regulatory changes, pricing shifts, and trust crises all create opportunities for challenger platforms to capture users from incumbents.
details.whyItMatters: Established platforms seem unassailable until a switching moment occurs. Identifying and capitalizing on these windows is essential for challengers. Preventing them is critical for incumbents defending market position.
takeaways: Technology shifts create natural switching moments between platforms
Trust crises can trigger mass user migration to alternatives
Pricing changes and policy shifts open windows for competitor entry

faq.question: What events have triggered major platform switching moments?
faq.answer: The mobile transition enabled Instagram to challenge Facebook. Cambridge Analytica's privacy scandal drove users to Signal. Twitter's ownership change drove users to Bluesky and Threads. Each crisis or transition opened windows that challengers exploited to capture users.

faq.question: How can challenger platforms prepare for switching moments?
faq.answer: Build the product and community in advance so it is ready when the moment arrives. Reduce friction in the onboarding process. Offer migration tools that import data from the incumbent. Time marketing pushes to coincide with the incumbent's missteps or transitions.
